title: ICE Issues Body Camera Requirement for Vehicle Stops After Resuming Operations
excerpt: Following two fatal traffic-stop shootings, ICE paused vehicle stops on July 14, Trump reversed the pause the next day, and on July 16 ICE issued new guidance requiring at least one body camera be worn during any vehicle stop — exposing that many officers lacked cameras.
content:
On July 14, 2026, ICE leadership issued an internal directive pausing Enforcement and Removal Operations vehicle stops nationwide after back-to-back fatal shootings in Houston (July 7) and Biddeford, Maine (July 13). The directive was intended as a temporary pause while officers received additional vehicle-stop training, according to sources.

On July 15, President Trump reversed the pause via Truth Social. On July 16, ICE issued new guidance requiring that at least one officer participating in a vehicle stop be wearing a body camera — immediately revealing that a majority of ICE officers still lacked cameras, effectively restricting how many stops could be conducted.

  • White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed more than half of ICE field offices had body cameras, with the remainder expected within 60 days.
  • One ICE source told reporters: "Unless someone has a body-worn camera, no vehicle stops can be made. Since the majority of officers do not have body-worn cameras, hardly any stops will be made."
  • Border Czar Tom Homan blamed the camera gap on Democrats, citing the DHS funding lapse earlier in the year.
  • The two shootings that prompted the policy had both occurred without any body camera footage.
source: Fox News / CBS News / Government Executive
